sub_agendas_items.minutes:

sub_agendas_items.title: Good Franco News
sub_agendas_items.minutes:
Member Pierre-Jérôme shared information relating to events for the Francophone community, such as Black History Month activities, the Gala de la Francophonie Plurielle happening on March 20, 2026, the Gala du Regroupement des gens d'affaires de la capitale nationale happening on May 7, 2026, and the Gala des Prix Bernard-Grandmaître happening on May 8, 2026.
Member Dupuis shared that, following repeated requests from the community, Recreation, Cultural and Facility Services continue to offer French recreational programming in the West part of the city. She shared that, while there is not yet a complete offer, recreational programs that were offered in French were sold out. 
Nathalie Lemire, Program Manager, French Language Services, highlighted that the city will nominate members of the Franco-Ontarian community for the Prix Bernard-Grandmaître, and further invited Members to provide suggestions for nominations to the Committee Coordinator. She also shared that the Mayor's Annual Francophone RendezVous will be held on March 27, 2026 and that Members will be receiving invitations to attend the event.
Chair Sénéchal shared a reminder to Members that they are invited to join Mayor Mark Sutcliffe and Councillor Stéphanie Plante for a breakfast organized on February 17, 2026 at City Hall.
Questions were raised with regard to the FLSAC End of Term Report and to the extent of comments and suggestions that are solicited from Members for the report. Vice-Chair Brownhill shared that the comments and suggestions being solicited will be in connection with the work of the FLSAC on the 2024-2026 Work Plan and related goals and objectives. She also shared that feedback from Members relating to their experience as Members of the FLSAC can be shared directly with French Language Services, the Program Manager for Council and Committee Services as well as with the Committee Coordinator.
